A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPO/RLHF study and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–I. Text, equations, algorithms, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix I report original XSum summarization experiments using DPO, IPO, and XPO, including comparative win rates and source-policy selection results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original summarization experiments and source-policy selection results in Tables 1–2 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: The TPO, TPS, and empirical TPO procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 3 relocates initialization and rewrites the UCB bonus equivalently. Revised optional guidance on choosing alpha does not change the algorithm's prescribed steps or default.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate XSum summarization under the same simulated preference environment. No dataset, domain, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: For each DPO, IPO, and XPO comparison, the baselines remain learning without transfer, purely exploiting ROUGE-Lsum, and purely exploiting T5-Large. Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix I retain the same model configurations, three training iterations, 10k training prompts per iteration, 10k evaluation prompts, Best-of-32 sampling, eight labeled responses per training prompt, and win-rate metric.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the same investigation of transfer-budget allocation and source-policy win rates across iterations. The supplementary analyses and qualitative Best-of-N comparison in Appendix I are unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 still report averages over three random seeds with 95% confidence levels. Figure 2 still averages allocation results over three trials. No uncertainty-reporting practice or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain every numerical entry, and Figure 2 retains the same plotted results. For example, iteration-3 DPO win rates remain 54.0 ± 1.2, 53.3 ± 1.5, and 50.6 ± 0.3 against the three listed baselines.

T1.justification: New Remark F.3 supplies an explicit late-time threshold and additional derivation for the existing TPO regret guarantee. The principal theorem and other proofs remain substantively unchanged; Corollaries 4.1 and 4.5 largely repackage existing results. The new remark contains an apparent confusion between bounded coverage and bounded cumulative transfer regret.

C1.justification: The central claims about regularization, policy coverage, TPO/self-transfer benefits, and empirical win-rate selection remain. Although v3 removes the detailed regret sentence from the abstract, its substance remains in the introduction and Section 4.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 reverses the recommendation for high-quality source rewards from larger alpha to smaller alpha, consistent with allocating the fraction 1−alpha to transfer. It also explicitly connects alpha decay to self-transfer learning. Other result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The corrected smaller-alpha recommendation revises hyperparameter-selection guidance. The default alpha = exp(−R/beta), Appendix I's implementation and hardware details, and the reproducibility statement's code access information are unchanged; no experimental setting change is established.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged. The new footnote about retained log-covering dependence reiterates a qualification already present in v2.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract, introduces TPO's name earlier, adds an upfront regret preview, and reorganizes the corollary discussion within Section 4. It fixes the unresolved corollary reference and updates affiliation/publication text. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithms 1 and 3 receive more compact formatting. Table 2 moves from page 35 to page 36, Figure 2 shifts vertically, and surrounding text reflows. The figures, table structures, captions, and visual encodings otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves navigation and corrects the alpha recommendation and broken corollary reference. However, new Remark F.3 claims Eq. (10) implies constant cumulative transfer regret, whereas bounded coverage in that equation yields an order-sqrt(t) bound. This apparent error leaves the added threshold argument unreliable as written. With unchanged empirical evidence, the benefits and this theoretical defect do not establish a clear net quality improvement.
